newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to build $50-mln jeans plant in Turkmenistan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to build $50-mln jeans plant in Turkmenistan.

text.p: Turkish company Gap Iplik will build a $49.6-million jeans factory in the former Soviet republic of Turkmenistan, a Turkmen government official said on Friday.
The plant will produce about 12 million square metres of denim cloth annually and produce five million pairs of jeans.

"The first step will see a credit of $17.5 million provided by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), which has not demanded a guarantee from the government," an official at Turkmenistan's textiles ministry told Reuters.
He said the government would hold 50 percent of shares in the plant, Gap Iplik 30 percent with the remaining 20 percent was to be held by the EBRD.

The plant, to be named after Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov, the focus of a personality cult in the mostly desert nation, will create around 1,000 jobs, with 80 percent of the workforce to be employed locally, the official said.
Turkmenistan, bordering Iran with a population of 3.6 million, produces cotton, but the official did not say whether Turkmen cotton would be used in the project.
